title: Advanced Electrical Load, Capacity, and Headroom
summary: Compare modeled load, capacity, utilization, headroom, and redundancy reserve.
objectives: Use units and assumptions to compare current and projected synthetic load with stated capacity.
Explain why capacity decisions must include redundancy and downstream dependencies.

vocab.def: Unused modeled capacity available before a stated limit is reached.
The portion of stated capacity currently in use.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: Calculations are synthetic and do not authorize system sizing or electrical work.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: For a scenario with 48 kW capacity, 31 kW current load, and 9 kW planned load, compute 40 kW projected load and 8 kW simple headroom. Then state whether redundancy reserve, measurement uncertainty, and shared dependencies require qualified review.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Show the expression, units, assumptions, and a safe escalation recommendation.

practice.prompt: What must accompany a modeled capacity number?
practice.answer: Units, assumptions, scenario limits, redundancy context, and uncertainty.

quiz.question: What is headroom?
options: Unused modeled capacity before a stated limit
quiz.answer: Unused modeled capacity before a stated limit

reflectionPrompt: What additional evidence would a qualified reviewer need?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
